result.corrected_claim: [trainloop-02] Confirmed on both the thesis-era snapshot (f633e44) and HEAD; the relevant source (StreamGraphDataset, LimitedStreamDataset, pyg_collate, make_stream_loader_for_split) is byte-identical in both. StreamGraphDataset sorts the file list and re-creates random.Random(42 + os.getpid()) at the start of every __iter__; with num_workers=0 the pid is constant across epochs, so every epoch yields exactly the same examples in the same order and, through DataLoader(bs=16, drop_last=False), the same minibatches. Shuffling is purely local: each consecutive block of max(128, 8*bs) items (128 at bs 8/16, 256 at bs 32) of the sorted-file concatenation is permuted in place. This holds regardless of --no_subset and for every (lr, bert_ratio) configuration of the sweep, which share one train_loader object per batch size. With the default --subset_frac 0.10, LimitedStreamDataset stops after int(0.1*N) items, so 90% of the training functions are never seen in any epoch; the subset is a fixed prefix of the lexicographically-first slice files, and because CPG_generator shuffles with seed 42 before select/clean/slice/merge (all order-preserving), that prefix is a random sample rather than label- or project-biased, and class weights (counted over all train files) remain appropriate. Across separate processes (e.g. hybrid vs CodeBERT-only arms) the subset membership differs only within the last partial 128-window (>=1-128/E, i.e. ~99% overlap at BigVul scale). Whether the Table 1 / Figure 2 runs passed --no_subset is not recorded anywhere: logs.log is empty, the W&B config logs no subset field, the thesis never mentions a subset, and the repo contains both a README example using --no_subset and plot directories named for 10%-subset runs. Effect: removes SGD's per-epoch batch-recomposition noise for both arms (200 epochs = 200 replays of one gradient sequence, modulo dropout 0.1/0.2 and the lr schedule), consistent with the memorisation pattern in F3; if the default was left on, 'trained on BigVul' is really 'trained on a fixed random 10% of BigVul train'. The magnitude of the F1 impact and any differential effect on the hybrid arm remain unmeasured.

Training data order comes from StreamGraphDataset.__iter__'s random.Random(42 + os.getpid()) with num_workers=0, so the order is fixed within a run but changes with every launch; R-GCN scatter ops on CUDA add further nondeterminism. (2) Arm identification: train() adds model.fusion.last_weights only when hasattr(model,'fusion') and the fusion has last_weights, otherwise adds 0.0; git -S shows weights_curve plotting, last_weights, CodeBERTOnly and --model_type were all introduced in f633e44 and the plotting removed in 72d02e9, so no committed hybrid variant could emit a flat-zero gate curve. plots_codebert_first/weights_curve is exactly 0.0 for 200 epochs, and its final val P≈0.52/R≈0.40 at τ=0.5 line up with Table 1's CodeBERT row (52.26/40.66), so it is the baseline arm. Caveat: both hybrid runs post-date f633e44 and pre-date the plot removal, but whether they used byte-identical code is not recorded, so the 2-point gap is suggestive rather than a controlled replicate. (4) Literature: steenhoek2023.txt lines 147-167 state std 2.9 on average, CodeBERT 2.78, LineVul 3.46, ReGVD 7.33, 95% within 5.8% (3 seeds, Devign dataset). (5) Thesis: all 7 pages read; no seed, repeat, interval or variance is mentioned; §4.4 describes one grid search and §5.1 Table 1 gives single numbers. (6) Arithmetic: a simulation with P=R=0.45 gives F1 sampling SD 1.9 pts at 500 test positives (1.3 at 1000, 2.4 at 300; the exact count is not recorded in the repo, but val/test loaders use the full splits), and with per-run SD 2.9 two draws from equal means differ by ≥1.89 about 64% of the time, so the claim's 'about half' is conservative. result.corrected_claim: Table 1 compares one training run per arm with no controlled randomness. In the thesis-era code (f633e44 lineage, the only version that has both the gate-weight plot and the CodeBERTOnly arm) and at HEAD, run.py sets no torch/numpy/random training seed and no deterministic flag; parameter init is fixed only as a side effect of torch.manual_seed(2020) at import of models/layers.py, data order comes from random.Random(42 + os.getpid()) with num_workers=0 (fixed within a run, different on every launch), and CUDA scatter ops are nondeterministic. plots_Elevneth is the hybrid run behind Figure 2 and plots_codebert_first is the CodeBERTOnly run (its gate curve is exactly 0.0 for 200 epochs, which train() writes only when the model has no .fusion; no committed hybrid variant lacks last_weights, and its final val P≈0.52/R≈0.40 match Table 1's CodeBERT row). Two hybrid runs with identical bs16/lr1e-4/ratio0.30 filenames (plots_12, plots_Elevneth; same code version not recorded but both from the same window) end at val F1@0.5 ≈0.43-0.44 vs ≈0.42 with qualitatively different gate dynamics; the baseline ends ≈0.45-0.46 and is still rising, with the same all-positive start and plateau level (its late P/R drift differs mildly). Steenhoek et al. report 3-seed test-F1 SD of 2.9 on average (CodeBERT 2.78, LineVul 3.46, ReGVD 7.33; 95% within ±5.8) on Devign; binomial test sampling alone gives an F1 SD of ≈1.3-2.4 points for 1000-300 test positives at P≈R≈0.45 (the thesis-era test loader uses the full split; the exact positive count is not recorded). With a per-run SD near 2.9, two runs with equal true means differ by ≥1.89 points about 64% of the time, and if the hybrid were truly 1.89 worse the baseline would still lose ≈18% of the time. The thesis mentions no seeds, repeats or intervals, so §5.1 ('falls slightly short') and §6 ('optimisation difficulties', 'structural information not effective enough') rest on a difference not distinguishable from noise; the evidence supports 'no measurable gain', not 'hybrid is worse'. This bears on neither the code nor the idea: the measurement cannot attribute.
